correctness.rationale: The source Problem 4 defines exactly 2/t times the conditional last-move ratio summed over reachable 0≤x≤vt. Reconstructed published Theorem 2 component stationary-phase asymptotics and shift of phase via phi′(u)=−alpha(u). The smooth positive-denominator periodic ratio R=q cos²theta/[sin²(theta−alpha)+q cos²theta] has phase average pminus(u)=1/2[1+u/(1+sqrt(1−2u²))], checked independently by high-precision direct quadrature at six allowed velocities. The published oscillatory-sum method (§12.4) removes nonzero Fourier modes on compact allowed intervals. In hidden compact intervals published Theorem 4/Sunada–Tate saddle rate gives r=(u+sqrt(2u²−1))/(1−u) and pplus=r²/(1+r²)=1/2+(1+sqrt(2u²−1))/(4u). Integrating pminus and pplus produces the two reported elementary branches. Delete an arbitrarily narrow wall strip via 0≤|a2/a|²≤1; no uniform wall asymptotic is assumed. Analytic branch differentiation and expansion give G(v*)=(1+sqrt2−log2)/4, common slope (2+sqrt2)/4, leading singular +2^(1/4)/3|v−v*|^(3/2), so C1 not C2. Fresh independent exact checker recurrence at T=3000 approaches the formula for v=0.2,0.55,0.7,0.72,0.8; at v=0.9 severe floating-point underflow limits corroboration but not analytic argument.
residual_risks: No uniform convergence rate through the wall, no v=1 result; hidden high-velocity direct floating-point checks can underflow. Compact-interval oscillatory-sum estimate is inherited from the primary paper, not independently reproved from first principles; must assume its theorem hypotheses.
